To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present an algorithm for learning policies for continuous control tasks that is able to solve many challenging tasks and is able to learn end-to-end policies from pixels.
we have developed an actor critic algorithm that can solve a wide range of simulated physics problems and that we have demonstrated its ability to learn from raw pixels.

(a) a simple deterministic policy gradient algorithm can be applied successfully to continuous control problems; (b) the same algorithm can also be used to train policies directly from raw pixel observations; (c) the learned policies can achieve performance competitive with the performance of a model-based optimal controller.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how we can learn to control a system with a large number of degrees of freedom directly from high dimensional sensory input, using only the reward signal as a supervisory signal.
the following question: can we learn to control complex, continuous action domains with deep neural networks?
developing algorithms that can solve complex problems in the real world.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our method, Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), is able to learn a variety of continuous control tasks with a high degree of robustness.
the algorithm presented in this paper is able to learn policies that solve a wide range of continuous control problems directly from high dimensional inputs.
our algorithm can learn a variety of complex control tasks directly from high dimensional sensory input, without the need for task specific features or hand engineered reward functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our algorithm is able to learn to perform a wide variety of complex tasks from high dimensional, raw sensory input solely with reinforcement.

we are able to train policies that are as good as those learned by a planning algorithm that has full knowledge of the environment, using a neural network that takes as input raw pixels, and is trained end to end, without any pre-processing, domain knowledge, or human intervention.
we are able to solve a variety of continuous control problems with a single algorithm, and we are able to learn from high dimensional sensory input.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the deep learning framework provides a unified way to solve a variety of control problems, and that it is possible to learn policies that are as good as or better than those found using classical planning methods, but without any domain knowledge.
deep reinforcement learning can scale to problems with high dimensional continuous action spaces.
deep reinforcement learning is now able to solve a wide variety of challenging continuous control tasks directly from high dimensional sensory input.
